gloss: to get carried away, to push one's luck

definitions.gloss: to get carried away, to push one's luck, to get cocky
definitions.explanation: To become overconfident or presumptuous after initial success or favorable treatment, often leading to behavior that others find annoying.

examples.japanese: {褒|ほ}められて{図|ず}に{乗|の}るな。
examples.english: Don't get carried away just because you were praised.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{少|すこ}し{成功|せいこう}すると、すぐ{図|ず}に{乗|の}る。
examples.english: He gets cocky as soon as he has a little success.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}に{気|き}に{入|い}られているからといって、{図|ず}に{乗|の}っていると{嫌|きら}われるよ。
examples.english: If you get carried away just because the boss likes you, people will start to dislike you.

notes:
USAGE:
This expression has a negative connotation and is often used as a warning or criticism. It describes someone who takes advantage of a favorable situation and becomes presumptuous.

ETYMOLOGY:
{図|ず} here refers to a plan or scheme going well. {乗|の}る means to ride or get on. So the expression literally means 'riding on one's successful plan,' implying overconfidence.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {調子|ちょうし}に{乗|の}る (to get carried away, to get on a roll)
- {天狗|てんぐ}になる (to become conceited)
